label: input token i at original position 4
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the letter i during the original phase, almost entirely at position t=4 (96% of activation mass). Every i at t=4 activates it (dev precision 1.0), whatever L is (L>=5), whether or not i appeared earlier, and whatever the neighbouring tokens are. It also fires weakly (about 0.1-0.2 of max) on some i inputs at t=3 and t=5, which make up the remaining ~16% of active steps but only 4% of mass. It never fires on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (including when i is fed back or output). Magnitude is highest at t=4 and much lower at the neighbouring positions; I found no other clear modulator.

issues: Every factual claim held up when I checked it. All activity is in the original phase, with none on the delimiter or in the copy phase. in_tok=i accounts for 100% of activation mass. t=4 carries 96% of mass, t=3 2.4% and t=5 1.6%. Mass is spread evenly over L=5..9, about 0.20 each.

Test-split misses: there are only 2 false positives, both at step 4 in sequences that contain repeated 3s. That looks like scattered noise. The 2690 missed steps (4% of mass) are all weak activations, about 0.07-0.13 of max, on i at t=3 or t=5. This matches what the explanation says.

The weak firing at t=3 and t=5 is a real but low-rate side effect, not something a predicate can usefully capture. i at t=3 fires about 10% of the time (precision 0.10, F1 0.10) and i at t=5 about 9% (F1 0.07). The rate at t=3 is about the same for L=4 and L>=5, so it is not a length pattern. Widening the predicate to t in 3..5 drops precision to 0.40 and F1 to 0.57, which is worse than the original 0.91.
The label does not overclaim: it matches the predicate, and the explanation itself mentions the weak activity at neighbouring positions.
